title: Prior art: Habiro's coloured Jones formula for the Borromean rings
html:
Habiro computes the Kauffman-bracket invariant of the Borromean rings with each component coloured by an element of the skein module of the solid torus. In the natural basis \{e_n\}, where e_n corresponds to the (n+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), the value \langle e_l, e_m, e_n\rangle is a finite sum over 0 \le i \le \min(l,m,n) of powers of (a - a^{-1}) times ratios of quantum factorials, symmetric in l, m, n [habiro2000, \S 3, p. 37]. In his modified basis \{R'_n\} the same invariant is diagonal: it is (a - a^{-1})^n\,[2n+1]!/[n]! when l = m = n and 0 otherwise [habiro2000, Prop. 7.1, p. 41].

The closed form of the Borromean Markov trace is the uncoloured case, so this is the published all-colours version of the same invariant, and Prop. 7.1 is a precise locator for the corpus's citations of this key. The paper works in the Kauffman variable a and its own normalisation; it does not compute the Markov trace in H_3(q), so matching the two at the fundamental colour needs the change of variables and framing to be checked first.
